interest: This document file note highlights early Japanese surveillance and intelligence operations in Burma concerning Allied and Chinese supply routes just as the Burma Road was being completed in late 1938. It illustrates the State Department's decimal filing and cross-referencing system, connecting Japanese military intelligence activities in Southeast Asia (file 894.20245C) to Chinese wartime logistics and munitions transit (file 893.24). For historians of the Second Sino-Japanese War and World War II, it marks the emerging strategic friction in Burma over Chinese supply corridors years before direct Japanese invasion.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department cross-reference sheet (Document File Note) dated December 23, 1938, referencing Despatch No. 139 from American Consul Austin C. Brady in Rangoon. Filed under the classification for Japanese military activities and espionage in Burma (894.20245C), it directs researchers to the primary document filed under 893.24/523 concerning the shipment of war supplies and munitions through Burma into China during the Second Sino-Japanese War.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing Despatch No. 139 from Rangoon concerning Japanese intelligence and activities regarding war shipments through Burma to China.
subfiles.summary: A State Department Document File Note cross-referencing Despatch No. 139 dated December 23, 1938, forwarded from the American consulate in Rangoon by Consul Brady. The underlying despatch, filed under 893.24/523, contains information regarding Japanese activities in Burma monitoring and potentially disrupting the transit of war materials intended for China. The sheet serves as an administrative marker within decimal classification 894.20245C for Japanese military and espionage activities in Burma.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Rangoon Despatch No. 139 on Japanese Activities in Burma
